events.title: The birth of Vatican Radio
events.shortBlurb: Marconi built it, and a pope's voice went out for the first time to all peoples and every creature…
body: On 12 February 1931 Pope Pius XI inaugurated the Vatican Radio, the Statio Radiophonica Vaticana, built for the Holy See within the Vatican Gardens by Guglielmo Marconi, the pioneer of wireless telegraphy, and blessed the instruments that were to carry the apostolic word to peoples far away.

The first voice carried on its waves was Marconi's, announcing that the Pope's voice could now be heard “simultaneously over the entire surface of the earth”; then Pius XI himself spoke in Latin, in the message Qui arcano Dei, opening with the words of Isaiah, “Hear, O islands, and listen, O distant peoples,” and addressing “all peoples and every creature” — the first broadcast of a pope in history.

From that day the Pope's Radio has carried the Gospel, the teaching of the successors of Peter, and the news of the Church to every continent, in more than forty languages; it stands today at the heart of Vatican News, ninety-five years on.

sources.text: Vatican, “February 12, 1931, the day Vatican Radio was born” (comunicazione.va)
